transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is work. I’m a claims processing clerk, so I’m supposed to sit at my workstation and get through claim reviews, but I keep getting up during the day even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish them.

It’s not even always for a real reason—I’ll stand up, walk over somewhere, maybe think of something else, and then I’m like, wait, I was supposed to be working on that file. And then the day kind of gets away from me. I mean, the office has this terrible coffee machine too, which doesn’t help because I’ll use that as an excuse sometimes, but… yeah, the getting up from my desk when I know I need to stay focused is what made me think I should probably talk to someone.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or losing focus on tasks outside of work, like at home or during other activities?

Yeah, I mean… it happens at work the most, but it’s not like it only happens there. If people near me start talking about another claim or I suddenly remember some random errand, my attention just kind of slides off whatever I’m reading. Then I realize I have no idea what the paragraph said, and I have to reread the same section a few times.

At home it’s similar sometimes, like I’ll be reading something or trying to look at a bill and then my brain jumps to, I don’t know, laundry detergent or whether I forgot to text someone back. It’s annoying because I’ll still be staring at the thing, but I’m not really taking it in.
Have you noticed that you've had trouble with staying focused or getting distracted easily for most of your life, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, I don’t think it’s totally new. Like, looking back, there were signs when I was a kid. In elementary school, teachers would say I was bright—my mom always liked that part—but then the rest of the note would be like, I lost worksheets, or I didn’t follow the instructions, or I needed reminders to actually finish the classwork.

I remember those little folders we had, the ones you were supposed to bring home and bring back signed—mine were always crumpled or missing. But yeah, the focus thing wasn’t something that just started recently. It’s just more obvious now because work is basically all paperwork.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot, even when you're not trying to get up for a specific reason?

Yeah, that’s kind of the big thing, honestly. I’ll be at my workstation and I know I’m supposed to just stay there and get through the claim reviews, but I keep getting up anyway.

Sometimes it’s not even like I have a real reason. I’ll just sort of stand up and move around, and then I’m halfway across the office thinking about something totally unrelated. Or I’ll tell myself I’m just grabbing coffee—though the coffee machine is awful, so I don’t even know why I do that—and then I come back and realize I lost the thread of what I was working on. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to avoid the work exactly, but I don’t stay put the way I’m supposed to.
Do you often feel a strong urge to do things without thinking them through first, or find yourself acting on impulse in ways that cause problems?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s, like, reckless or always doing things without thinking. I mean, I’ll sometimes say something and then later think, “That came out weird,” but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

When you say acting on impulse, do you mean like spending money suddenly or interrupting people or… I don’t know, making big decisions? Because I don’t think that’s a huge thing for me. I can overthink stuff, actually. But then again, sometimes I’ll do little things without really planning—like grabbing my phone or clicking around—and suddenly I’m off on some other thing. Sorry, I’m kind of wandering. I guess I haven’t noticed major problems from impulse stuff the way I have with focus.
Do you often feel physically restless or like you can't sit still, even in situations where you're expected to, like during meetings or when riding in a car?

Yeah, in stuff like trainings or longer team meetings, I definitely notice it. I’ll be trying to look like I’m paying attention, but my leg is bouncing under the table, or I’m clicking a pen without realizing it, or I keep shifting around in the chair.

It’s not like I’m trying to be disruptive. Sometimes I’ll notice someone glance over and then I’m like, oh, right, stop doing that. But then a few minutes later I’m doing it again. Especially if the meeting drags on—like those policy update trainings where they use the same slide template forever. Sorry, that’s not really the point, but yeah, sitting still for those is hard.
